name: Prince Che
strengths: Che anchors at the point with true 305 mass — absorbs single blocks and holds gap integrity so linebackers can scrape clean.
Che occupies doubles on inside zone, tying up center/guard and forcing cutbacks with two-gap width.
Che presses with early hands and can push the pocket when pad level stays right — drives the interior into the QB’s lap.
Che shows functional range for his size — works down the line and finishes backside pursuits outside his original alignment.
weaknesses: Che rises at the snap at times and gets washed on combo blocks when pad level climbs.
Che’s pass rush is still mostly power — needs more counters beyond the bull rush on obvious passing downs.
comparison: Che comps to Vita Vea — thick 6-3 / 305 interior mold; occupies doubles, pushes the pocket, and holds the point with mass (size-matched within ~1–2" of Che’s 6-3 / 305 frame).
projection: Che projects as Year 1 interior rotation who develops into starting nose/3T snaps, then competes for every-down DT — ceiling as a space-eating SEC disruptor who occupies doubles and frees the second level.
schemeFit: Che fits as a nose/3T who two-gaps, occupies, and creates second-level clean-up.
insiderNotes: Che is a thick 6-3 / 305 interior who occupies doubles, anchors the point, and pushes the pocket when he wins early with hands. Gerald Chatman has Florida’s offer on him; Clemson leads the On3 board while UF stays second and pressing.
staffNotes: Vault film desk re-verified 2026-08-24 from Hudl embed (Thomas County Central soph reel). Comp size-matched within ~1–2" — not a Florida-alum default. Beat Desk Open.

angle: Lead with Chatman offer + interior priority; mass/occupy tape; calm Clemson board lead mid-post.
